newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Germany denies proposing talks with drug lords.
newsitem.headline: Germany denies proposing talks with drug lords.

text.p: The German embassy denied on Tuesday that Bonn had suggested the United States join in or approve talks aimed at brokering a "peace deal" between the Colombian government and Cali cartel drug lords.

U.S. Ambassador Myles Frechette said in an interview published on Sunday in Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper that the suggestion was made last July by German spymaster Bernd Schmidbauer, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's chief of intelligence services.
"(Schmidbauer) sent emissaries to ask the American government if it was willing to see talks (with the heads of the Cali cartel). We replied in an official statement that we weren't," Frechette said.

The German embassy statement, effectively calling Frechette a liar, said the idea of talks with the Cali cartel had never come up in any exchange between representatives of the U.S. and German governments.
"The German government has never had the intention of arranging talks with the Cali cartel or any other drug cartel," the statement said.

It said the United States had, however, been invited by Germany to "cooperate constructively" in efforts to arrange peace talks between the government of Colombia and leftist guerrillas fighting to overthrow it.
